correctness.rationale: The published structure theorem gives, for every level n, a suffix tiled by the three blocks f(h^n(a)) or f(g(h^n(a))). With ternary weight d(0)=-1,d(1)=0,d(2)=1, direct calculation gives Delta(f(a))=d(a) and shows that both h and g preserve d. Hence every complete level-n block has imbalance at most one, while every such block has length at least 2^n. Decomposing a factor into complete blocks plus two boundary fragments gives |Delta(u)|<=2^{-n}|u|+C_n. Taking long-factor limsups and then n to infinity proves uniform half-density. The verifier independently replays the morphism identities and block growth.

value.rationale: The result extracts a global statistical rigidity from a structural theorem whose stated purpose is repetition avoidance. It applies to every infinite word in the extremal low-repetition rich class, not only to a canonical construction, and strengthens ordinary prefix frequency to uniform frequency over all long factors. The quantitative family |Delta(u)|<=2^{-n}|u|+C_n exposes the mechanism and can constrain future factor-frequency and dynamical analyses without asserting a stronger bounded-balance property.
